plain.text: "I will give thanks to you, LORD, with all my heart; I will tell of all your wonderful deeds. I will be glad and rejoice in you." David praises God because his enemies have turned back. God has upheld his cause, sitting on his throne as a righteous judge, and has rebuked the nations.

The LORD reigns forever and judges the world in righteousness. "The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble. Those who know your name trust in you, for you, LORD, have never forsaken those who seek you." Sing praises to the LORD; he does not ignore the cry of the afflicted.

David asks God to have mercy and lift him up from the gates of death, so he can declare God's praises. The nations have fallen into the pit they dug; the wicked are trapped by their own work. "But God will never forget the needy; the hope of the afflicted will never perish."
"Arise, LORD, do not let mortals triumph; let the nations be judged in your presence. Strike them with terror, LORD; let the nations know they are only human."

summary.bigIdea: God is a fair judge and a safe refuge for the oppressed; he never forgets the needy.
points: David thanks God with his whole heart for his wonderful deeds.
"The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble."
God never forgets the needy, and their hope will not perish.
summary.reflection: Who do you know who is oppressed or in need? How could you pray for them, or help?
